_about: written judgement about what each model is for. SOURCE, not derived: analyze-usecase
carries it into data/usecase.json beside the numbers, and never overwrites it.
the numbers lead. every `evidence` entry names a facet and the percentile the model
holds on it WITHIN this registry -- p79 means it beat 79% of the registry models that
carry the same facet, not 79% of every model in the world. `claim` marks a number the
model published about itself, which analyze-self-report measures as running about +0.9
high, and which is the weakest evidence here.
confidence is about the EVIDENCE, not the model: high means several independent
third-party sources agree, medium means one source or a thin sample, low means nobody
has measured it and this is the card plus whatever the forums said.

MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.5.one_liner: a tool-use model with unusually clean javascript and typescript play, now superseded by m2.7 in its own family.
MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.5.notes: artificial analysis has it flagged deprecated, and m2.7 beats it on every axis both carry, so it is worth running only if the 0.42gib smaller quant matters.

MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7.one_liner: the registry's best instruction follower and long-context reader, at the cost of the slowest decode in its size class.
MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7.notes: both forums that discuss it are unanimously positive, but on small samples (49 and 24 mentions). speed sits at p19, so a long agent loop pays for the quality.

Qwen/Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B.one_liner: a world model for agent environments rather than an assistant: it predicts the next environment state, it does not do your task.
Qwen/Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B.notes: no benchmark in this corpus measures what it does, so it is unranked rather than bad. the card is the only description of its job.
evidence: no facet carried by any source
card: covers seven agent interaction domains in one model

Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct.one_liner: a small fill-in-the-middle coder: the one model here tuned for autocomplete rather than conversation.
Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct.notes: it is bottom-quartile on every measured axis, which is the expected shape for a 30b a3b completion model and not a reason to avoid it at the job it was built for -- nothing here measures fim.

Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-Next.one_liner: resolves real merged pull requests well above what its benchmark indices predict, and decodes fast while doing it.
use_for: coding agents on a latency budget
Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-Next.notes: the gap is the interesting part: swe-rebench p69 against aa coding p29. swe-rebench builds its tasks from pull requests merged after release, so that number is the one that cannot have been trained against. forum reception is mixed (hf-discussions 33% approval).

Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B.one_liner: too small to be a general assistant; its use here is as a speculative drafter and a smoke test.
Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B.notes: bottom of every axis it carries, which is what an 0.8b model is. it is in the registry because a drafter has to come from somewhere.

Qwen/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B.one_liner: a well-liked long-context generalist that follows instructions better than it codes.
Qwen/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B.notes: 82 reddit mentions at 91% approval is one of the better reception numbers in the registry, and it is the a10b that people actually run rather than the 397b they cannot.

Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B.one_liner: a dense 27b that fixes real bugs: top-sixth on swe-rebench, and strong on javascript and python play.
Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B.notes: arena rating sits at p27 while its task scores are top-quartile, which is the usual shape of a model tuned for work rather than for being pleasant to talk to.

Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B.one_liner: a fast a3b tool-caller with the best python play in its size class and a weak sense of planning.
Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B.notes: gbench decision-making p16 against tau2 p83 is a real split: it calls tools reliably and chooses badly what to do with them.

Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B.one_liner: the strongest qwen3.5 on nearly every axis, and the one whose weights most people cannot fit.
Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B.notes: perfect python play over the games gbench ran it on, and swe-rebench p92. barely discussed anywhere, which is a size problem rather than a quality one.

Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B.one_liner: a small tool-caller: it holds up on tau2 and falls away everywhere else.
use_for: agentic / tool use at small scale
Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B.notes: tau2 p67 with mmmu, osworld and scicode at p0 is a narrow shape -- fine as a router or a cheap first pass, not as the model that finishes the job.

Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B.one_liner: the most-discussed local model in the corpus, and the registry's best planner among dense 27b weights.
Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B.notes: 311 reddit mentions at 86% approval, and the phrase that keeps coming back is daily driver. gbench decision-making p84 is unusual for its size. slow decode at p11 is the price.

Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.one_liner: a popular a3b tool-caller that reads well and plans badly.
Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.notes: the second most discussed model here (141 reddit mentions, 82% approval) and one of the weakest planners measured: gbench decision p11 and webdev arena p0.

Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B.one_liner: the strongest dense model in the registry on measured axes, and the current default answer for a single 27b that has to do everything.
Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B.notes: gbench has not played it yet, so its evidence is aa plus its own card plus 208 reddit mentions at 89% approval. the template defaults thinking to xhigh, which costs 15k-52k thinking tokens in reported traces against qwen3.6's 3k.

XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5.one_liner: a coding and physics model with the best rust play measured here, let down by one-shot coding and decode speed.
XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5.notes: do not confuse it with mimo v2.5 pro, which is a different model with a different swe-rebench score; the tables mismapped exactly that pair once.

deepreinforce-ai/Ornith-1.0-35B.one_liner: an agentic-coding model whose only numbers are its own, and whose two forums disagree completely about it.
use_for: agentic coding, on its own claims
avoid_for: anything where the claim needs to be independently checked
deepreinforce-ai/Ornith-1.0-35B.notes: 16 huggingface discussion mentions at 0% approval against 13 reddit mentions at 100%. that split usually means it works when it loads and often does not load. no third-party benchmark carries it.

deepreinforce-ai/Ornith-1.0-9B.one_liner: the 9b of the same self-improving family, with claims that put it in the bottom third of the claimants.
deepreinforce-ai/Ornith-1.0-9B.notes: nothing third-party has measured it and nobody discusses it. everything known about it is its own card.

deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731.one_liner: the registry's strongest all-rounder: top decile on science, coding, long context and physics at once, and the most discussed model after qwen3.6.
deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731.notes: at UD-IQ3_XXS it is 97gib, so on a 128gb box it fits with a drafter and little else. best go play measured here at 82%.

google/embeddinggemma-300M.one_liner: an embedding model: it emits vectors, not text, and no benchmark in this corpus scores it.
evidence: no facet carried by any source

google/functiongemma-270m-it.one_liner: a 270m model tuned for one job: turning a request into a function call.
google/functiongemma-270m-it.notes: the only registry entry whose sole capability tag is `tools`. nothing here measures routing accuracy, so it is unranked.
evidence: no facet carried by any source

google/gemma-4-12B-it.one_liner: a small multimodal assistant that follows instructions well for its size and reasons poorly.
google/gemma-4-12B-it.notes: hle and critpt at p0 against ifbench p75 is the honest shape: it does what it is told, it does not work things out.

google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it.one_liner: a likeable one-shot coder and chat model that falls over as soon as it has to hold a tool loop.
google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it.notes: aa agentic p0 with gbench one-shot p76 is as clean a split as this corpus contains: ask it for a whole answer, not for a sequence of steps.

google/gemma-4-31B-it.one_liner: the best-received chat model in the registry by arena rating, and a strong one-shot coder in python and javascript.
google/gemma-4-31B-it.notes: arena p87 and gbench one-shot p82 against agentic weakness; also the slowest decode measured here at p0. it writes well and does not drive.

google/gemma-4-E2B-it.one_liner: an on-device gemma: small enough to run anywhere, weak on every axis measured here.

google/gemma-4-E4B-it.one_liner: the larger on-device gemma; the same shape as e2b with a little more of everything.

inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash.one_liner: a hybrid-reasoning moe that lands in the top third on agentic and coding at 5.1b active parameters.
inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash.notes: thinly discussed (12 reddit mentions) and not on the gbench board, so the evidence is artificial analysis plus its own card.

meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B.one_liner: the best long-context reader in the registry, and a strong game player, with an operational reputation problem.
meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B.notes: aa long-context reasoning p94 and gbench overall p84, but 43 huggingface discussion mentions at 0% approval against 111 reddit mentions at 73%. read the discussion tab before committing: that pattern is usually a quant that does not load rather than a model that cannot think.

mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B.one_liner: a fast dense 128b that calls tools well and does no science at all.
mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B.notes: critpt at p0 twice over, from both aa and epoch, is a consistent verdict rather than one bad run. perfect javascript play over the games it was given.

moonshotai/Kimi-K3.one_liner: the most capable model in this registry on every reasoning axis, and at 553gib the one that costs the most to find that out.
avoid_for: anything that has to fit in 128gb
moonshotai/Kimi-K3.notes: p97 on six axes at once. its thinking knob is `thinking_effort`, whose guard rejects the `medium` its own injected prose says it supports. decode is p4, the second slowest here.

nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF.one_liner: fast and good at contest maths on its own card, weak on everything a third party measured.
nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF.notes: aime 98.2 is its own claim at p91; the third-party numbers around it sit at p20-25 and its long-context and swe scores are p0. the gap between claim and measurement is the story of this entry.

nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B.one_liner: a physics-leaning 120b that gbench ranks at the bottom of the board it plays on.
nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B.notes: gbench overall and decision-making both at p0 against critpt p76. its card recommends temp 1.0 across every task including tool calling, and the registry runs it colder anyway -- `upstream-tool-use` records what the vendor actually said.

nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B.one_liner: the fastest model in the registry by a wide margin, and it spends all of that speed being average.
nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B.notes: 298 tokens/s at p96 with intelligence at p27. worth it when volume matters more than the answer; not otherwise.

openai/gpt-oss-120b.one_liner: fast, widely run, and beaten on quality by most of what it sits beside -- but the best pure language play measured here.
openai/gpt-oss-120b.notes: 100% gbench success in go, c++ and java against aa coding and agentic near the bottom, and an arena rating at p0. it compiles what it is asked for and loses the argument about what to ask for.

openai/gpt-oss-20b.one_liner: the small gpt-oss: quick, cheap, and out of its depth on anything agentic.

poolside/Laguna-S-2.1.one_liner: a one-shot coder: it writes a whole program well and cannot run an agent loop.
poolside/Laguna-S-2.1.notes: gbench one-shot p71 against agentic p8 -- the widest such split in the corpus. hf-discussions approval of 33% against reddit's 82% points at quant problems rather than model problems.

prism-ml/Bonsai-27B-gguf.one_liner: 27b-class reasoning in binary weights: an efficiency experiment, and the worst-received model in the corpus.
prism-ml/Bonsai-27B-gguf.notes: 123 huggingface discussion mentions at 0% approval and 34 reddit mentions at 14%. no benchmark carries it, so the reception IS the evidence. the retention curve in build-tables does not model binary weights, which is why it carries native_low_bpw.
evidence: no facet carried by any source

prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-27B-gguf.one_liner: the ternary sibling of bonsai, with the same reception and the same absence of measurement.
prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-27B-gguf.notes: 70 huggingface mentions at 0% approval. ternary weights are outside the quantization curve this repo fits, so a bpw comparison against it is meaningless.
evidence: no facet carried by any source

stepfun-ai/Step-3.7-Flash.one_liner: the most reliable tool-caller measured here, and a capable planner, that cannot write a program in one go.
stepfun-ai/Step-3.7-Flash.notes: tau2 0.985 at p96 with gbench one-shot coding at p0 is the mirror image of gemma 4 26b. give it tools and steps, not a blank file.

tencent/Hy3.one_liner: top-decile on reasoning and the best-rated model here by human preference, with a gbench sample too thin to quote.
tencent/Hy3.notes: gbench has played it 7 games over 25 matches, which is why its gscore is marked thin rather than used. 48 reddit mentions at 93% approval is the best reception in the registry.

thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small.one_liner: a science and physics specialist: p91 on critpt, omniscience and scicode at once.
thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small.notes: do not read the flagship inkling's gbench score onto this model -- the generated tables did exactly that once. it is not on the gbench board at all.

upstage/Solar-Open2-250B.one_liner: an office-and-document moe that scores best on physics and scientific code, and that nobody in these forums discusses.
upstage/Solar-Open2-250B.notes: its template collapses medium, high and xhigh into one branch, so the thinking knob has one effective setting under three names, and the `none` its card documents changes nothing at all.

Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo.one_liner: a single-stream diffusion transformer for fast text-to-image, run here with a separate vae and text encoder.
Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo.notes: needs three weights rather than one: the diffusion model, a vae, and a qwen3-4b text encoder. no benchmark in this corpus scores image models.

baidu/ERNIE-Image-Turbo.one_liner: baidu's distilled text-to-image release, built for few-step generation.

ideogram-ai/ideogram-4-fp8.one_liner: ideogram 4 at fp8, whose family is known for rendering legible text inside images.

krea/Krea-2-Raw.one_liner: the raw krea 2 checkpoint: more steps, fewer shortcuts, aimed at image quality over latency.
use_for: text to image where quality matters more than speed

krea/Krea-2-Turbo.one_liner: the distilled krea 2: the same family in few steps, for interactive use.

fishaudio/s2-pro.one_liner: a text-to-speech model with inline control of prosody and emotion, trained on 10m+ hours.
fishaudio/s2-pro.notes: its chat template drops a developer message and accepts unlimited leading system messages, which is unusual for a speech model and recorded in turns anyway.
evidence: card: fine-grained inline control of prosody and emotion

hexgrad/Kokoro-82M.one_liner: 82m parameters of text-to-speech that holds up against much larger models, and the cheapest voice here to run.
evidence: card: comparable quality to larger models at 82m parameters

khimaros/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-CustomVoice.one_liner: the smallest qwen3-tts custom-voice build: voice cloning at 0.6b, quantized for llama.cpp.

khimaros/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base-GGUF.one_liner: the 1.7b qwen3-tts base voice, covering ten major languages and several dialects.
avoid_for: voice cloning without the customvoice build

khimaros/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice.one_liner: the 1.7b qwen3-tts tuned for cloning a supplied voice.
evidence: card: voice cloning and voice design support

khimaros/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-VoiceDesign.one_liner: the qwen3-tts build that invents a voice from a description rather than copying a sample.
use_for: voice design from a text prompt

mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602.one_liner: realtime multilingual speech transcription, and one of the first open models to claim parity with closed asr.
evidence: card: realtime, multilingual, accuracy comparable to closed models

openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo.one_liner: the distilled whisper large v3: the default open asr, faster than the model it came from.
evidence: card: state of the art asr and speech translation
